figures.caption: Figure 1: Multiple neural timescales and the MTS-SLDS framework. A Neural activity can switch between regimes with different characteristic timescales (here τ1, τ2 and τ3, τ4). The pooled autocorrelation of such a signal is not well described by a single exponential, and a multi-exponential fit summarizes the decay without attributing components to regimes. B MTS-SLDS models Poisson spike counts or Gaussian signals as observations of a latent state xt whose linear dynamics Azt are selected by a discrete regime zt. Figure 2: Timescale recovery in stationary and switching systems with Gaussian and Poisson observations. A Estimated timescales under stationary (K = 1, Nτ = 2), where hollow markers represent different runs, and filled markers show medians. aABC shows the posterior median and 50%/95% credible intervals. B Estimated timescales under switching (K = 2, Nτ = 3 per regime) dynamics, where circles denote latent modes of timescales, and dots dentoe medians. C Example held-out latent continuous states and regime inference in switching dynamics. D, E Timescale MAPE versus Gaussian SNR and mean Poisson counts in switching dynamics, respectively, where shading denotes interquartile ranges and dashed lines denotes the reference 10% error level.

Figure 3: Multiple timescale structure of V4 activity during fixation. A Fixation task and data analysis schematic. B Predictive gains over a constant-rate Poisson baseline: cross-validation (left, mean ± SE) and paired test trials at H = 8 (right). C Example trial spike train, one-step rate predictions, and cumulative log-likelihood difference between MTS-SLDS and SLDS. D Observed and model-generated pooled autocorrelations and residuals over 100 ms fitting window, where values in legend denote RMSE of each method. E Timescale estimates of different methods. For state-space models, small markers show 5-fold estimates and diamonds show medians. ACF-exp and aABC fits show estimates from pooled population autocorrelation, and aABC displays posterior medians and 50%/95% credible intervals.

Figure 4: Task-related timescales in somatosensory Area 2. A Reach trajectories and onset-aligned movement speed during active reaching (purple) and passive perturbations (orange). B Held-out predictive log-likelihood gain versus latent dimension, where gray shading marks the selected H = 6. C Inferred movement-regime probabilities with MTS-SLDS and SLDS. D Latent timescale spectra for pre-movement and movement regimes in the 20-300-ms analysis range. E Slowest effective timescales across regimes demonstrate different patterns between MTS-SLDS and SLDS. F Geometric mean of timescales for real and time-shuffled recordings. Lines in E,F connect paired estimates. G Behavioral decay times (individual estimates and means) compared with median slowest movement-regime timescales. MTS-SLDS inferred timescales are in close agreement with behavior decay times.

Figure 5: Pooling can obscure latent temporal modes in a single recording. A Per-mode recovery fractions from three-exponential ACF fits in the setting. B Mean BIC-selected exponential order in both count settings. A and B reuse the same generated recording at every pooling level, with 30 channel draws per level; full-pooling repetitions vary only optimization. C Effective timescales of one- and two-exponential fits at full pooling in the setting. Marker size indicates relative ACF amplitude; the lowest-residual fit at each order is displayed. D Dotted lines indicate the true order or timescales.

Figure 6: Effects of initialization and fitting configuration. A Timescale MAPE for K = 2 under RC-Laplace-EM with moment or ssm initialization. The upper strip shows iterations to reach 15% MAPE across ten seeds (triangle, threshold not reached). B, C Minimum per-regime recall and timescale MAPE for K = 3 under the same initialization comparison. Curves in A-C show example runs; right-hand points in B, C show final outcomes across seeds. D Timescale MAPE before and after RC-Laplace-EM or Laplace-EM fitting from moment-based starts. Thick lines highlight one seed; light lines show the others.

Figure 8: A,B Decay times and frequencies recovered by MTS-SLDS for oscillatory dynamics. C Recovery of three decay timescales by MTS-SLDS, SLDS, and ACF-exp. Black horizontal lines indicate ground truth, where red and blue markers denote MTS-SLDS and SLDS, respectively, and gray diamonds denote ACF-exp.

Figure 9: Held-out V4 prediction at H = 8. (A) Raw spike counts from the same trial 59. (B,C) Observed and predicted rates averaged across channels and for a selected channel example (channel 9). (D) Cumulative predictive log-likelihood difference between MTS-SLDS and SLDS. (E) Per-channel one-step predictive gains over the constant-rate Poisson baseline.

Figure 10: Effective timescales and exponential-fit diagnostics in V4. (a) Estimates from H = 2 state-space models and two-timescale aABC. Points show fold fits, diamonds show medians, and aABC intervals. (b) Components from one-, two-, and three-exponential ACF fits across fitting windows.

Figure 11: Held-out trial activity prediction and regime inference in Area 2. A Spike counts from an example held-out active trial. B,C Observed smoothed firing rates (black) and estimates from MTS-SLDS (red) and SLDS (blue dashed), pooled across channels B and for a single channel C. D Movement-regime posterior probabilities across held-out trials during active reaching (left) and passive perturbations (right), where each row represents one trial and vertical dashed lines mark movement onset.
Figure 12: Timescales estimated by sPCF-EM are shown for pre-movement and movement regimes during active (red) and passive (blue) conditions.
